note: Updated Sun 4 Oct 2026 (weekend research refresh -- all markets closed since Fri 2 Oct's close; next session Mon 5 Oct). No new US/HK/SG/JP trading session occurred over the weekend, so headline levels are unchanged from Fri 2 Oct (S&P 7,722.72 +0.73%, Nasdaq 27,190.86 +1.19% intraday record, VIX 15.31 -6.59%, GLD 380.14 -0.68%, SLV ~59.98/54.74 -1.23%/-0.51%, GDX 87.78 +1.20%, WTI 91.11 -1.90%, Brent 102.25). This run's incremental research confirms the Oct-hold repricing is a pause, not a pivot: CME FedWatch puts Oct 27-28 hold odds at ~82.8% (Kalshi ~78%, hike ~21%, cut ~1%), but prediction markets still price a December hike, consistent with the Fed's first hike since 2023 having only just landed in September. The 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 5.34% intraday 30 Sep-1 Oct, a fresh 24-year (since-2002) high, on energy-driven inflation concern; 10-year TIPS real yields near 2.65-2.89% are the highest in roughly 18 years, while 10Y breakeven inflation sits near 2.28-2.36% -- rates markets are pricing persistent inflation risk even as the Fed pauses. DXY dipped modestly on the NFP miss (~101.9, -0.17/-0.20% on 2 Oct) but remains up roughly 3% over the past month on the September-hike/December-hike framing. Euro area HICP printed 3.8% y/y, a three-year high, reinforcing a hawkish ECB alongside BOJ's already-hawkish path (hiked to 1.25% 18 Sep; Tokyo core CPI 2.7% y/y keeps a 29-30 Oct hike live). Credit stays bifurcated: CCC-and-below OAS crossed the formal 1,007bps distressed threshold on 30 Sep (widest since the 2023 SVB collapse; ~1,215bps per ICE BofA on 1 Oct) even as broad HY (~270-320bps) and IG (sub-100bps, richest since 1998) spreads sit near multi-decade tights. Weekend geopolitics: the US is moving a third carrier strike group plus ~2,000 Marines toward the Middle East, Russia struck a second Kyiv bridge, and the G7 agreed Friday to release up to 100M barrels of diesel/crude over four months after Washington had floated a fuel-export ban; China's major refiners suspended most refined-fuel exports for October; OPEC+'s JMMC met Sunday 4 Oct and was expected to hold November output targets unchanged. China's Golden Week holiday (1-7 Oct) keeps mainland markets and Stock Connect flows suspended through 7 Oct. The Trump-Xi rare-earth/tariff truce was extended only two months, to 10 Jan 2027 (not the 6-12 months many hoped for), leaving Taiwan/chips friction and a near-term re-escalation risk unresolved. AI capex supercycle intact: 2026 hyperscaler capex guidance has risen toward $700-780B combined (vs ~$410-416B in 2025), with Meta raising full-year guidance to $125-145B; SMH is up roughly 69% YTD (vs Nvidia +23%), a concentration/crowding risk flagged by several desks. Government shutdown risk is off the table through 11 Dec 2026 (2 Sep stopgap, signed into law, House 370-48); a 24% shutdown-odds estimate attaches to the Dec 11-31 window. Week ahead: ISM services Mon 5 Oct, FOMC minutes Wed 7 Oct, Q3 bank earnings begin 13 Oct (JPM) and 14 Oct (WFC).

macro.regime: Risk-on relief rally meets a hawkish-paused (not pivoted) Fed and energy-driven inflation anxiety
macro.narrative: September Non-Farm Payrolls missed badly (+29K vs ~84-90K consensus, unemployment up to 4.2%, wage growth cooling to +0.1% m/m/+3.0% y/y -- the lowest since May 2021 -- with a net -60K two-month revision to July/August), pushing CME FedWatch odds of an October 27-28 hold to roughly 83% (Kalshi ~78%) and driving a broad Friday rally into the weekend: S&P500 +0.73% to 7,722.72, Nasdaq +1.19% to 27,190.86 (an intraday record), VIX collapsing -6.59% to 15.31. Yet the medium-term rate path stays genuinely hawkish, not dovish: the Fed only resumed hiking in September (its first hike since 2023) and prediction markets still price a December increase, while the 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 5.34% intraday on 30 Sep-1 Oct, a fresh 24-year high, on energy-driven inflation concern reinforced by euro-area HICP at 3.8% y/y (a three-year high) and Tokyo core CPI at 2.7% y/y -- both above target and strengthening the ECB's and BOJ's (hiked to 1.25% 18 Sep, next meeting 29-30 Oct) hawkish cases. Credit is bifurcated: CCC-and-below OAS crossed the formal 1,007bps distressed threshold on 30 Sep -- its widest since the 2023 SVB collapse -- even as broad HY/IG spreads sit near multi-decade tights (~270-320bps HY, sub-100bps IG), a classic late-cycle quality divergence. Energy geopolitics intensified into the weekend: the US is moving a third carrier strike group and roughly 2,000 Marines toward the Middle East, Russia struck a second Kyiv bridge, and the G7 agreed to release up to 100M barrels of diesel/crude over four months after Washington had threatened a fuel-export ban, even as OPEC+'s Sunday 4 Oct JMMC was expected to hold November output steady and Brent held near $102. Markets head into a news-dense week (ISM services Monday, FOMC minutes Wednesday, Q3 bank earnings starting 13 Oct) still digesting a soft-labor/sticky-inflation mix that keeps the Fed's pause fragile rather than a genuine pivot.
